builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
summary: This regime replaces full fine-tuning and teacher-trace reasoning supervision with parameter-efficient LoRA trained on labels alone. It requires only single-GPU-scale training memory and avoids the cost of generating teacher traces, though a teacher model is needed if reasoning variants are compared; the tradeoff is that adding reasoning supervision underperforms labels-only training in-domain. What can fail is that results are demonstrated on Qwen3-8B financial tasks only, so the ranking may not transfer to other base models, domains, or tasks where explicit reasoning is required at inference.
rationale: For a constrained-infrastructure team doing domain adaptation, response-only LoRA is the cheapest regime and the paper shows it dominates reasoning-trace variants in-domain while preserving general capabilities.
technique: Response-only LoRA fine-tuning for domain adaptation

claims.statement: This regime replaces full fine-tuning and teacher-trace reasoning supervision with parameter-efficient LoRA trained on labels alone. It requires only single-GPU-scale training memory and avoids the cost of generating teacher traces, though a teacher model is needed if reasoning variants are compared; the tradeoff is that adding reasoning supervision underperforms labels-only training in-domain. What can fail is that results are demonstrated on Qwen3-8B financial tasks only, so the ranking may not transfer to other base models, domains, or tasks where explicit reasoning is required at inference.

Response-only LoRA yields the largest in-domain gains in calibration and argmax accuracy relative to reasoning-supervision regimes, while retaining general capabilities near the frozen model; reasoning-trace supervision improves MMLU-Pro only slightly and dual-adapter training adds no gain.
